features.optics-qsfp28: installation guide: "six fixed 40/100-Gigabit QSFP28 uplink ports that support combinations of 10-, 25-, 40-, 50-, and 100-Gigabit connectivity".
features.optics-sfp28: installation guide: "48 10/25-Gigabit SFP+ downlink ports that support 1-Gigabit, 10-Gigabit, and 25-Gigabit Ethernet". SFP-10G-T-X is supported only in a stated checkerboard of ports, with the neighbours limited to passive copper.
features.usb-limit: USB 2.0 devices that use less than 2.5 W (0.5 A inclusive of surge current)

physical.acoustics: 48.5 dBA at 40% fan speed, 64.9 dBA at 70% fan speed, and 77.8 dBA at 100% fan speed
physical.weight-note: 7.8 kg (17.2 lb) without power supplies or fans

power.power-supply-options: 500W AC, 650W AC, 930W DC, or 1200W HVAC/HVDC (up to 2)

ac-port-side-exhaust.description: Dual NXA-PAC-650W-PE supplies and four NXA-FAN-30CFM-F fan modules - port-side exhaust airflow, blue latches. The installation guide's Overview table gives the colours.

ac-port-side-intake.description: Dual NXA-PAC-650W-PI supplies and four NXA-FAN-30CFM-B fan modules - port-side intake airflow, burgundy latches

description: 48x 1/10/25G SFP28 and 6x 40/100G QSFP28 1RU data-centre leaf switch on Cisco's Cloud Scale LSE ASIC, running NX-OS or ACI. All fifty-four ports and the BCN, STS and ENV lamps are on the port side; two power supplies, four fan modules, the console, both management ports and the USB are on the other. Ports number 1-54 and run DOWN each column - odd on the top row, even beneath it. Ships port-side intake (burgundy modules) or port-side exhaust (blue). End-of-sale was announced in August 2021.

gaps.wanted: The data sheet (c78-742283, Table 2) gives the width as 17.3 in (43.9 cm); the installation guide's Switch Dimensions table gives 17.5 inches (44.5 cm). Same measure, same scope, different value. 439.4 is carried because a real-unit photograph, corrected for perspective on the SFP cage pitch, closes on it to 0.14%. A ruler across a chassis settles it.

A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The installation guide's two overview figures show a side wall in three-quarter view and call out six screw holes for the rack-mount brackets and two for the grounding lug on it, and the mounting chapter shows the lid the same way; none is flat and none can be measured. Each of the four carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked.

What the two round dark features at the upper left of the port side are. The stencil render and the port-side photograph both show two of them side by side at about 5.4 and 8.9 mm from the left edge, 11.8 mm down, above the BCN lamp, with no legend. The guide's callout for this corner names only BCN, STS and ENV. They are not drawn: a lamp, a button and a hole look the same at this resolution.

What the eight dashes in each QSFP28 band are. Between the up and down port lamps each band carries two rows of four short dark dashes, clear in the stencil and resolved in the photograph. They are in the right place and number to be per-lane breakout lamps for the two cages, and no staged document says so: the guide's LED appendix describes port lamps as triangles and nothing else. They are drawn as marks on the band and carry no state.

The meaning of the row printed under each QSFP28 pair: a square, an up and a down triangle, and a second square. Drawn as printed, from the stencil, and explained nowhere in the guide or the data sheet.

The colours and blink patterns of BCN, STS, ENV and the port lamps. The installation guide's LED appendix gives tables for the fan module and the power supply and one sentence for the chassis; the startup procedure adds only that STS "is green" after initialisation. Searched both staged documents for BCN, ENV and "port LED".

Faces for the other supplies this switch accepts. The guide lists N9K-PUV-1200W (HVAC/ HVDC, white), UCSC-PSU-930WDC (green), UCS-PSU-6332-DC (grey), NXA-PDC-930W-PI and NXA-PDC-930W-PE, and the data sheet adds NXA-PAC-500W-PI and NXA-PAC-500W-PE. The only supply any staged image shows is the 650 W AC one, so that is the only one the bays accept here.

A stated or measured size for the supply and the fan module. No staged document gives either in millimetres; both are read off the stencil render, which is 1.7% narrow on the port side where a photograph can check it.

The vertical step between the two SFP rows. 16.2 mm is the stencil's proportion; the registry's stacked-cage figure is 15.0. A square-on photograph with the full face height in frame would settle it and every other y on this face.

attrs.redundancy-note: Installation guide, Overview: four fan modules of two rotors each. The switch runs normally with one rotor failed in any one module; with more than one rotor failed it warns and powers down in two minutes. The guide states no N+1 figure for whole modules, so none is written here.

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band cluster at the right of the power-supply side - an RJ-45 console port, an RJ-45 and an SFP management port of which one is active at a time, and a USB Type-A port for saving and copying files. Three media, one purpose: reaching the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: installation guide: "Power supply modules (two - One for operations and one for redundancy [1+1])". Slot 1 is on the left and slot 2 on the right.

name: n9k-c93180yc-ex

colour.note: The face colour is the median of a 1700-pixel sample of bare plate along the foot of the stencil render's port side, #d0d2cf. The port-side photograph is lit too dimly to sample - the same plate reads #615d52 there over 10000 pixels - so it confirms only that the face is a light grey with dark printing and brighter bands between the cage rows. The band and ink values are chosen against the stencil by eye and are not sampled.

gate-1.note: NEITHER FULL-FACE IMAGE IS AN ELEVATION TO BE MEASURED WHOLE, AND THE TWO FAIL DIFFERENTLY. The stencil render is flat, but scaled on its own SFP pitch (54.0 px per 14.25 mm) its body between the ear folds is 431.7 mm against the data sheet's 439.4: 1.7% narrow, and its 170 px height is 44.9 mm against 43.7. The port-side photograph is a perspective view from the left: the SFP pitch reads 51.9 px in the first group of eight, 50.75 in the second and 49.1 in the third. THE PHOTOGRAPH IS THE ONE USED FOR X, WITH THE PERSPECTIVE FITTED AND THEN PROVED. A quadratic through those three local scales, integrated from the left edge of the face, puts the right edge at 438.8 mm - 0.14% from the stated 439.4, on a quantity the fit never saw. The same integration reads the three QSFP28 openings 19.95, 19.84 and 19.73 mm wide against the registry's 20.0, and each SFP group 114.0 to 114.1 against 8 x 14.25.

interface-names.note: mgmt0 IS THE INSTALLATION GUIDE'S: its setup chapter asks for "the Management (Mgmt0) interface" and says "The RJ-45 and/or SFP management ports provide out-of-band management" - one interface, two connectors - so both placements take the name mgmt0 and the export carries it once, typed from the RJ-45. Ethernet1/1 TO Ethernet1/54 IS NOT IN EITHER STAGED CISCO DOCUMENT: searched the installation guide and the data sheet for "Ethernet1/" and found nothing, because port naming lives in the NX-OS interfaces configuration guide, which is not staged. The names are the NetBox devicetype-library device type for this model, a community file, which lists Ethernet1/1 to Ethernet1/54 in faceplate order with 1 to 48 SFP28 and 49 to 54 QSFP28, and they are the slot/port form NX-OS uses on every fixed Nexus 9300. ESTIMATED IS THE WORD FOR THE WEAKER HALF: mgmt0 is stated by Cisco and the Ethernet names are read from a community file, so the entry as a whole is no better than that.

port-lamps.note: Installation guide, Switch Chassis LEDs: "The port LEDs appear as triangles pointing up or down to the nearest port." Both images show one up and one down triangle per SFP column in the band between the rows, and one of each at the two ends of each QSFP28 band. THE GUIDE GIVES NO COLOUR TABLE for port lamps or for BCN, STS and ENV; the states here are the legend and on, nothing more.

port-order.note: Read off the port-side photograph and the stencil, which agree. Each SFP column prints two numerals on one baseline above the upper cage with an up and a down triangle between them - "1 (up)(down) 2" - so the odd port is the upper cage. The QSFP28 columns print "49 (up)" and "(down) 50" the same way. The installation guide numbers nothing in its figures; the data sheet's architecture text gives ports 1 to 48 and 49 to 54.

power.note: Data sheet Table 2 and the installation guide's Switch Power Input Requirements agree: 210 W typical, 470 W maximum, "(AC or DC)". The data sheet's footnote says both "are based on input drawn from the power circuit", so these are the switch's draw at the inlet and not a supply rating. Neither document names the configuration or ambient. Heat is printed two ways - 1604 BTU/hr in the data sheet, "1603.706" per hour in the guide - and the data sheet's rounding is carried.

rear-face.note: Every x and y on the power-supply side is a fraction of the stencil render, scaled so the body between the ear folds is 439.4 mm across and 43.7 down. The stencil is the only flat picture of this face. WHAT IS ON IT AND IN WHAT ORDER IS CONFIRMED by the real-unit photograph and by the guide's callouts 1 to 7: supply 1, four fans with fan 1 at the left, supply 2, then the console jack over the RJ-45 management jack, the SFP management port, the USB port stood on end, and the BCN and STS lamps with a screw between them. The printed strips beside the supplies read P1, F1, F2 and P2, F4, F3 in the stencil; the photograph resolves the same six labels. THE TWO STACKED JACKS MIRROR: the stencil draws the console jack's contacts along the foot of its opening and the management jack's along the top, with the management jack's two lamp windows in its lower corners, so the upper jack is keyway-up and the lower keyway-down.

sources.note: Five sources, none of them committed. (1) Cisco Nexus 93180YC-EX NX-OS Mode Hardware Installation Guide, 72 pages, the 2023 capture: the overview callouts, the specification appendix B and the LED appendix C. (2) Cisco Nexus 9300-EX Series Switches Data Sheet, c78-742283, the 2025 capture: Table 2 specifications, Tables 4 to 6. (3) Cisco's end-of-sale notice EOL14472. (4) The NetBox devicetype-library front and rear elevations of this model, which are renders of Cisco's own Visio stencil, 1841 x 170 px. (5) Photographs of real units from resale listings: one port-side photograph at 1600 x 1200 and one power-supply-side photograph at 1600 x 603 with blue modules. THE GUIDE'S OWN FIGURES ARE THREE-QUARTER VIEWS at 718 x 168 px and carry callouts, not geometry. No vendor 3D model was found.

stack-orientation.note: Both rows of SFP cages show their contacts toward the band between the rows, and the port lamps in that band point up to the upper cage and down to the lower, in the stencil and in the port-side photograph alike. So a row pair is the upper cage upright over the lower turned 180, the library's stack convention, here read off the device for the SFP rows. The QSFP28 pairs take the same rule; their lamps point the same way.

the-width.note: THE TWO DOCUMENTS DISAGREE AND THE DATA SHEET IS CARRIED. Data sheet Table 2: "1.72 x 17.3 x 22.5 in. (4.4 x 43.9 x 57.1 cm)". Installation guide, Switch Dimensions: width "17.5 inches (44.5 cm)". 17.3 in is 439.4 mm and the perspective-corrected photograph closes on it to 0.14% with the SFP pitch as its only ruler; 444.5 would leave 5.7 mm unaccounted for. Neither figure includes the rack brackets, which are a separate kit (NXK-ACC-KIT-1RU). Height 1.72 in is 43.7 mm and depth 22.5 in is 571.5 mm, the same in both documents. See the gap.

the-x-axis.note: From that integration, with the 0.6 mm residual split between the two margins. The SFP groups start at 10.9, 129.1 and 247.3: two gutters of 4.2 mm, read 4.16 and 4.28. THE STENCIL DRAWS THOSE GUTTERS AT 1.85 mm and the left margin at 9.8; the photograph of the real unit is followed, and the three gutter-and-margin differences add up to the 7.7 mm by which the stencil body is narrow. The QSFP28 openings start at 366.9, 391.3 and 415.7, a 24.4 mm step read 24.7 and 24.1.

the-y-axis.note: NOT MEASURED. The photograph is taken from above and its vertical axis carries no scale. Every y is a fraction of the stencil render's 170 px height applied to the stated 43.7 mm: SFP rows at 7.2 and 23.4, QSFP28 rows at 7.3 and 24.1, the numerals on one baseline at 5.0, the two rows of square vent holes at 37.6 and 41.0. The SFP row step that gives is 16.2 mm where the registry's belly-to-belly figure is 15.0; the photograph shows a tall bright band between the rows, so the stencil's step is kept and recorded as an estimate.
